=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- .claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md:65; workflow-templates/.claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md:65 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: The checker prompt says "Never use GraphQL-backed `gh` commands" but instructs the checker to use `gh run list`, which is GraphQL-backed and can fail with HTTP 403 in the checker’s web session environment.
  WHY: When the review-run probe fails, the checker cannot determine whether a review run is active and may fail or misclassify a conflicted/red PR as stuck.

- .claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md:65-66 (step 3 logic) | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: The checker is instructed to inspect labels on linked issues but has no mechanism to discover which issues are linked to the PR.
  WHY: A linked issue carrying `ai:review-blocked`, `ai:review-autofix-failed`, or `ai:needs-human` can be missed because the PR API response does not provide linked-issue labels.

- .claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md:13 (step 4) and 137 (workflow pick — actual line 24 for step 8, 29 for step 9) | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: Step 4’s collision handling says to append `-2`, `-3`, … on collision, but `git checkout -B <branch>` silently overwrites an existing local branch and the procedure does not define checks for existing local or remote work before resetting it.
  WHY: A leftover phase branch with unmerged commits can be silently reset and lose work, while unspecified workflow-file selection can dispatch the wrong customized workflow or produce an avoidable alert.

- .claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md:44–45, 47 (Check-in Loop Routines); line 54 (Fallbacks) | severity=high | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The Check-in Loop does not specify cleanup, persistence, or failure handling for Routines when the session ends abnormally or `create_trigger` fails mid-operation.
  WHY: An interrupted session can leave orphaned Routines that later fire against stale or incorrect plan/session state and accumulate across runs.

- .claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md (and the byte-identical workflow-templates/.claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md), step 9 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: The shared step 9 instruction passes `-f tracking_issue=0 -f pr_number=0` to both validation workflows even though the consumer `ai-validate.yml` does not declare a `pr_number` input.
  WHY: Consumer validation dispatch rejects the unknown `pr_number` input, so validation is never dispatched and the project stalls at the validation gate.

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- .claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md
  Line or code reference: 65 (same in workflow-templates/.claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md:65)
  severity=MAJOR
  confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The checker prompt says "Never use GraphQL-backed `gh` commands" but then instructs the checker to use `gh run list -R <owner>/<repo> --workflow=<review workflow file> --branch=<head branch> -L 3 --json status` for the review run. `gh run list` is GraphQL-backed and will fail with HTTP 403 in the checker's web session environment.
  WHY: The checker session is created as `create_new_session_on_fire: true` with `model: claude-sonnet-5` — a web-based Claude Code session. Per CLAUDE.md §23.D, "Claude Code Web's agent proxy serves only a pinned set of GraphQL operations and rejects the rest with HTTP 403, so GraphQL-backed commands (`gh pr list`, `gh issue list`, `gh search`) can fail." `gh run list` falls into this category. When the review-run probe fails, the checker cannot determine whether a review run is active. This breaks the "stuck" detection in step 3: a conflicted/red PR older than 6 hours with an active review run should NOT be reported as stuck, but the checker cannot verify the review-run status and may either fail the check entirely or misclassify the PR. The REST equivalent is `gh api "repos/<owner>/<repo>/actions/runs?branch=<head branch>&per_page=3"`.

- .claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md
  Line or code reference: 65-66 (step 3 logic)
  severity=NIT
  confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The checker's "done waiting" decision says to check whether "its linked issue carries ai:review-blocked / ai:review-autofix-failed / ai:needs-human" but the checker has no mechanism to discover which issues are linked to the PR. The PR API call `gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/pulls/<N>` returns the PR's own labels, not linked-issue labels. Discovering linked issues requires either GraphQL (disallowed by the same prompt) or regex-parsing the PR body for `Fixes/Closes/Resolves #N` patterns (not instructed).
  WHY: When a linked issue carries `ai:review-blocked` but the PR itself does not, the checker will incorrectly report the PR as "still healthy" rather than "blocked" because it cannot check the linked issue's labels. The checker needs to either parse the PR body for linked issue references from the already-fetched PR data, or the main command must pre-resolve the linked issue number and fill it into the checker prompt template as an additional placeholder.
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- .claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md
  Line or code reference: lines 13 (step 4) and 137 (workflow pick — actual line 24 for step 8, 29 for step 9)
  severity=NIT
  confidence=4
  PROBLEM: Step 4's collision handling "(append `-2`, `-3`, … on collision)" is misleading. `git checkout -B <branch>` silently overwrites an existing local branch — it does NOT detect collision. If a previous run left an unmerged `claude/implement-plan-<slug>-phase-<n>` branch with WIP, the next invocation would lose those commits on `-B` reset before the agent could opt for `-2`/`-3`. The procedure says nothing about (a) checking whether the branch already exists locally or on the remote, (b) inspecting whether it carries unmerged work that would be lost, or (c) the operational rule that decides when to fall back to `-2` vs. when to force-push. Similarly, steps 8 and 9 say "pick the one that exists" for the security-audit / validate workflow file but do not specify the concrete strategy — `gh workflow list --json name` + name match, or a `gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/contents/.github/workflows` listing, or just try-then-fallback — leaving the agent to improvise.
  WHY: An agent that takes the `-B` instruction literally against a leftover phase-1 branch will silently discard unmerged phase-1 work, then push the new phase-2 branch on top of an outdated base, breaking the one-phase-per-PR chain the procedure is built on. An agent that tries both workflow names in random order will either leak a `not found` Telegram alert or, worse, accidentally dispatch the wrong workflow on a consumer repo whose `.github/workflows/` has been customised.

- .claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md
  Line or code reference: lines 44–45, 47 (Check-in Loop Routines); line 54 (Fallbacks)
  severity=MAJOR
  confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The Check-in Loop arms two claude-code-remote Routines (poke + 3h-cron Sonnet checker) per phase and per gate cycle, with `create_new_session_on_fire: true`. The text says the session disarms them via `delete_trigger` on a clean merged wake (step 7) and on the completion PR merge (step 10), but does not specify behaviour if the session itself ends abnormally (operator closes Claude Code mid-wait, container restart, network drop mid-`create_trigger`). The Routines would persist across sessions; the next invocation does `list_triggers` and removes stale Routines — but only AFTER step 4 has already produced a branch, so a stale checker firing between sessions could pokes the wrong branch. There is no pre-arming guard, no Routine-id persistence requirement on the log line before the API call returns, and no fail-open behaviour described for `create_trigger` returning an error mid-flow. The Fallback section only handles tool absence, not tool-failure mid-operation.
  WHY: An interrupted session leaves two orphaned Routines. The stale checker will fire 3 hours later in a throwaway Sonnet session, call `fire_trigger` on a poke id that no longer corresponds to the live session, and either do nothing (best case) or — if the operator re-armed manually — pokes the wrong plan's session. The session-local cleanup contract is implicit; nothing in the procedure prevents orphaned Routines from accumulating across many plans run over many weeks, which the orchestrator audit at `agents.md:25.D` would later flag.
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_2 ===
- .claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md (and the byte-identical workflow-templates/.claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md), step 9
  Line or code reference: "Dispatch the validate workflow — `internal-validate.yml` here, `ai-validate.yml` in consumers ... with `-f tracking_issue=0 -f pr_number=0`"
  severity=MAJOR
  confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The consumer wrapper `workflow-templates/ai-validate.yml` does not declare a `pr_number` input. Its `workflow_dispatch.inputs` block (lines 6-27) declares only `tracking_issue`, `compose_file`, `validation_timeout`, and `alert_msg_level`, and its `with:` block (lines 35-39) forwards only those four to the reusable `validate.yml` — it never passes `pr_number` through. By contrast `internal-validate.yml` (this repo) does declare `pr_number` (line 11) and forwards it (line 42). So the single `-f tracking_issue=0 -f pr_number=0` instruction is valid for `internal-validate.yml` but invalid for `ai-validate.yml`.
  WHY: `gh workflow run` client-validates every `-f`/`-F` key against the target workflow's declared `workflow_dispatch.inputs` and rejects unknown keys; in a consumer repo `gh workflow run ai-validate.yml -f tracking_issue=0 -f pr_number=0` errors on the undeclared `pr_number` input, so the validation step (step 9) never dispatches and the project stalls at the validation gate in every consumer repo. The reusable `validate.yml` already defaults `pr_number` to "0" (line 16) when `tracking_issue=0`, so `-f pr_number=0` is also redundant on the internal path; dropping it from the shared instruction fixes both repos without changing behavior. The "if neither exists, record Validation: not wired" escape does not apply because `ai-validate.yml` does exist — it merely rejects the extra flag.
=== END FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_2 ===
